title: Mike Van Wyck is a big dummy
summary: NH rebuts a viral Instagram rant by PED user 'Big Mike' Van Wyck, who claimed naturals hate steroid users out of jealousy and cowardice. NH calls this projection and argues that natural pride rests on health and longevity. His 'chicken dinner' analogy explains why naturals must push back when PED users try to normalize drug use in a mostly natural community.
claims: The claim that naturals criticize PED users out of jealousy is projection; the PED user is the insecure one, because his results depend on an outside substance while the natural depends only on himself
Men often confuse risk-taking with bravery, like the friend who calls you weak for not drinking himself to death
Most PED users started taking steroids out of insecurity about their body or manhood, and the drugs never fix that insecurity
Mocking naturals for not risking their health is like mocking someone who refuses to play frisbee on the highway
Blood tests do not make PED use safer; being aware of the danger does not reduce it
Lifting to fix insecurity is good while PEDs are not, because natural bodybuilding promotes health and enhanced bodybuilding moves you closer to death with every injection
The TRT argument is the 'smart' PED users' attempt to borrow scientific legitimacy, and it is easy to dismiss
PED advocates keep moving the goalposts: first PEDs were not dangerous, then slightly dangerous, now 'we all die anyway', the same YOLO logic as hard drug users
Naturals stay natural to have more healthy years with the people they love and to protect and guide them, not for a gold plaque on their tombstone
PED users have the freedom to use, which he would not outlaw, but freedom does not exempt them from social judgment
PED users act like 'cry bullies': macho bravado until they face factual criticism, then they play victim and claim their freedom is under attack
About 99% of PED influencers' followers are natural lifters; naturals only ask them to stop lying and leave the natural community alone
When a PED user copes publicly, his audience reassures him and slowly copies him, which creates more PED users

Chicken dinner analogy: nine kids eat chicken and broccoli and one eats McDonald's, and that is balanced; it becomes dangerous only when the McDonald's kid says it is healthier and calls the others cowards, so someone must challenge him
Arguing against PEDs on the grounds of pleasure loses every time; keep the debate on health and facts
PED influencers built the supplement and powder market on the natural community, using drug-made gains to sell programs and products
Natural influencers who defend PED users do it partly from a misguided idea of tolerance and partly to keep collaborations, audience and money
Pride in being natural is what keeps you natural; without it there is no reason not to take drugs
PED rhetoric works on young men because it promises fast muscle and appeals to emotion rather than logic
